title: 도로명주소 읽기: 로/길·건물번호, (아파트) 동·호 찾기
summary: Learn to quickly locate and say the road name ending with ro/gil plus the building number, and, when present, apartment building/unit numbers (dong/ho) in Korean written addresses from print, texts, or map apps.
objective: By the end of this worksheet, learners can 1) spot and read the road name that ends with ro/gil plus the building number, and 2) find and say apartment dong and ho quickly and accurately.
exercises: Write the road name + building number and the 동/층/호 (write 없음 if there is none): 광주 북구 무지개로 58
Write the road name + building number and the 동/층/호 (write 없음 if there is none): 부산 해운대구 바다숲로45번길 17, 3층 (우동)

Write how to say this address from the road name through 호, reading the numbers with Sino-Korean numbers (write them in Hangul). Leave out the region and the parentheses at the end: 경기 성남시 분당구 푸른숲로 146, 101동 402호 (정자동, 초록아파트)
Write the road name + building number and the 동/층/호 (write 없음 if there is none): 대전 유성구 별빛로 29, 5동 (관평동, 새빛연구단지)

This address is written in the everyday informal style. Write how to say it from the road name to the end, including the building name before 호 and leaving out the region, reading the numbers with Sino-Korean numbers (write them in Hangul): 서울 마포구 달빛로12번길 8, 해오름빌라 203호

sections.heading: Road-name addresses at a glance
paragraphs: A Korean address is read in three parts: region (시/도, 시/군/구) + road name and building number + (for apartments) 동·호.

Example: in ‘서울 종로구 햇살로17길 12, 202호 (부암동, 한빛빌라)’, ‘햇살로17길 12’ is the road name and building number, and ‘202호’ is the unit number. The parentheses at the end hold the neighborhood (법정동) and the building name.

sections.heading: Finding 로/길 (ro/gil) and the building number
paragraphs: Road names usually end in ‘…로’ (ro) or ‘…길’ (gil), including ‘…번길’ (beon-gil). The number right after the road name is the building number.
How to read them: ‘세종대로 백십’, ‘햇살로 십칠길 십이’. Read the numbers clearly with Sino-Korean place units (천/백/십).

sections.heading: Finding apartment 동·호 (dong/ho)
paragraphs: In apartments, officetels and similar buildings, the detailed address (동·층·호) comes after the comma. ‘동’ is the building number within the complex, ‘층’ is the floor, and ‘호’ is the unit (room) number.
Official pattern: ‘…, 101동 1203호 (○○동, ○○아파트)’ or ‘…, 1203호 (○○동, ○○오피스텔)’ (sometimes there is no 동). The building name goes in the parentheses at the end, together with the neighborhood (법정동).
Everyday informal style: many people write the building name before 동·호, e.g. ‘…, 초록아파트 101동 1203호’. You will often see this on packages and in text messages, but it is not the official format.

sections.heading: Tips for finding them quickly
paragraphs: 1) First, find the end of the road name, the last ‘로’ or ‘길/번길’. For branch roads like ‘…로17길’ or ‘…로45번길’, the number stuck to the word is part of the road name. The number after the space is the building number.

2) Look for ‘동’, ‘층’ and ‘호’ right after the comma (in the informal style, after the building name). The words in the parentheses at the end are the neighborhood and building name, not the unit. If there is no 동·층·호, say ‘없음’ (none).
3) When speaking, say ‘road name + building number’ first, then ‘동·호’.

sections.heading: Practice instructions
paragraphs: Answer format for finding: ‘road name building number; 동·층·호’ or ‘road name building number; 없음’ (none). For reading: say only the road name + building number and then the 동·호 (plus the building name if it is written before 동·호, as in the informal style); leave out the region and the parentheses at the end. Write the numbers in Hangul, e.g. ‘세종대로 백십’.

note: The example addresses were made for practice. Apart from ‘세종대로 110’, the road names, buildings and units are made up and do not refer to real places.
